note: No presentation. A watch is set by a party the room has authorized to read it, exactly as a listing is; a host account or session is never the authority in this family.

An address that is not a DID. The host sends the signal as a Trust Task over a transport the address's DID document advertises; a URL would make the host call an endpoint the member chose, and a push token would hand the host the device's push channel.
`cancel: false`. Only `true` is meaningful; an arming request omits the member.
A lease beyond 30 days. A watch that outlives the member's interest keeps sending to an address nobody reads.
`live: false`. Only `true` is meaningful; a one-shot watch omits the member, so that a request says one thing in one way.
`live` as a string. It is a boolean that only `true` satisfies; a host never has to read meaning into a spelling.
A response that does not say whether the watch is armed — the one thing the member needs to know.
`live: false` in a response. A one-shot watch omits the member; only its presence says a watch is live, so that a host implementing 0.1, which never writes it, is read correctly.
